chunk_map.heading: H1/lede: Map the access surface, own the delta
Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk
Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map
Point the skill at your feature
Kick off the pass, then work the other window
Phase 2: Read the map back before you decide the delta
Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed
Push back until the reason names your codebase
Phase 4: Add the context header a cold reader needs

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 4 L52 "Switch to your m3-quality window now." — "m3-quality" is not named earlier in THIS file (chunk 0's Window widget names only "m3-security"). Verified via module include-order: `earn-the-trust.md` line 33 lists `[Exercise: Open the side quest]` immediately before this file (line 37); `open-the-side-quest.md` lines 39/42 have the student run `/rename m3-quality` on the second worktree session there. Session-artifact + module-include-order carve-outs both cover it. Also checked: "STRIDE" (chunk 0 L11, reused chunks 1/8/9) is arc-earned — named in `earn-the-trust.md`'s What-You'll-Learn bullet 2, which the module renders before this exercise's include; "the delta" (title + chunks 1/6/7/9) self-earns at chunk 0 ("own the *delta*", "What you build"); "The countermove from M1" (chunk 1 L18) unpacks in the same sentence and "M1" is a carved-out module name. No unresolved pronoun/demonstrative in any chunk.

Closest candidate: chunk 3 L47 "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close is the best input here." This locates a fact by module-close position, but `earn-the-trust.md` Prework (line 12: "you noted the path at M2 close") states the identical fact and renders before this exercise in module include order — carve-out, not an invented positional pointer. "Author your test-strategy skill" (chunk 4 L52) and "the STRIDE exercise" (chunk 9 L94) are both named by title, matching real sibling files (`author-test-strategy-skill.md`, `threat-model-with-stride.md`) listed in the module's Start Here order — named, not positional ("the next exercise").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close" (chunk 3 L47): confirmed live in `earn-the-trust.md` Prework L12. "m3-quality" / the side-quest window (chunk 4 L52 implies it exists): confirmed `open-the-side-quest.md` exists and precedes this file in the module's Start Here order, and its body names that session `m3-quality` at L39/L42. `curriculum/evals/arc-read.ae101.md:23` independently records this exact plan-path connection as arc-verified ("Plan-file promise under-delivered — FIXED. map-the-access-surface names the M2-noted plan path as the best input."). No dead beat reference found.

Closest candidate: chunk 7 "Push back until the reason names your codebase" (33 words, 1 bullet per `check-slide-size.js --report`) — one bullet, but it carries a full self-standing instruction plus a worked contrast example ("'The billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry...' beats 'webhooks need auth.'"), not a bare wait-state bullet. Chunk 4 (96 words, 2 bullets) is also substantive: names the two-window move and gives the concrete switch instruction. No chunk is content-free or purely context-dependent.

chunk 2 "Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map" (L22-39): header promises two actions — run the skill on the student's feature, save the map. Chunk content (L26-39, current body: the `/skills` check, "you should see access-control-analysis and stride listed under User," "Ask Claude to list its installed skills, with storage location and context-load status," prompt-1) only performs skill discovery/listing. The actual invoke-on-feature-and-save-to-temp-directory action lives under the NEXT `##` heading, "Point the skill at your feature" (L41-47, prompt-2), which carries no Phase-1-continued marker. Under the sequential slide read, the Phase 1 slide's content does not deliver what its own header claims. Harm: a Slides-view reader could take the Phase 1 header as already covering invoke+save and be thrown when that action appears on a differently-titled slide with no phase link. Non-blocking per template partition (rule 6 explicitly listed as blocking:false) — the slide is still followable, just misdescribed by its own header.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retitle chunk 2 to what it actually delivers (e.g. "Phase 1: Confirm the skill is on hand"), or fold the invoke-and-save prompt into this chunk so Phase 1's header lands on the content it names.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all five sub-items across all 10 chunks. (a) `grep -niE 'not [a-z].*\. not [a-z].*\.'` on body.txt → 0 hits. (b) manual read: no anaphora/epistrophe triples. (c) self-grading-superlative grep (`one of the most|most useful|most important|game.?chang|powerful move|critical(ly)?|essential`) → 0 hits in body; closest candidate chunk 0 L11 "STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling" is a stance claim about the field (the file's own backing block classifies it as a position, not a value-prop claim about this exercise), not a self-grading superlative. (d) no number-with-retraction pattern; the only numbers are widget timings (20/7/3 min) with no hedge attached. (e) no abstraction-noun stack or empty-leg verb triplet — prose stays concrete (e.g. "the billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections)\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--map-the-access-surface.body.txt` → all 9 hits are on "surface"/"access-surface"/"surface map"; zero hits for firing/compendium/forcing-function/beat/mood/Connections in the body region. "Surface" here is the exercise's own domain term (attack/access-surface security analysis — the module's own Start Here question uses it too: "what's the surface you're most nervous about a teammate missing"), not the compendium's banned authorial-jargon sense ("writing surface"). "Delta" is ordinary engineering usage.

No bolded-lead monoculture found; other bullets are plain prose. Accept-note applies; not flagged.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 8 of 9 `##` headings are unambiguously imperative ("Take the ranked ten...", "Point the skill at your feature", "Kick off the pass...", "Push back until...") or "Phase N:" + imperative. Closest candidate: chunk 9 "What this sets up" (L92) is neither imperative nor a Phase label, but asserts no generalizable law (unlike the compendium's declarative specimens, e.g. "Anything can be reverse-engineered") — it is a navigational segue naming what the next exercise depends on, matching the orientation-header carve-out ("You are here"). `grep -rn '^## What this sets up' curriculum/exercises/*.md` finds the identical heading reused verbatim in `author-test-strategy-skill.md`, confirming a repeated closer-label convention in the exercise library rather than a one-off ambiguity. Rule postdates the template's explicit blocking list (only enumerates 1-14); applying the template's stated principle ("I cannot follow this" = blocking, "this could be tighter" = TODO) directly — a genre mismatch on a non-declarative closer is not a comprehension failure. Classified non-blocking here, judge-owned classification since the template list doesn't name it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet against the three classes. Chunk 9's closer (L92-94, "the sow-here-reap-at-STRIDE motivation") is explicitly accept-noted in the maintainer block: "Carded and kept (Antti 2026-08-25): the *What this sets up* slide... do not re-card." Closest un-accepted candidate: chunk 4 L51 "That wait is the two-window move Module 3 installs" names the module's own pattern (self-referential flavor) but stays in-class because it fuses to a concrete instruction in the same sentence ("kick off a long task in one window, do active work in the other, come back when the first lands") and is the FIRST operationalization of the move in this file, not a redundant re-announcement — unlike the banned specimens, which carry no instruction at all. The maintainer's own 2026-08-25 lean-pass note (L100) independently confirms this rule was actively applied to this file (cut "aphorism kicker, §16c", a "forward plant", a "restatement"); a re-check of the current body against the same three classes found no further instance. Rule postdates the template's explicit blocking list; classified non-blocking under the same stated principle as rule 15 — judge-owned classification.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.

No maintainer provenance note of the shape "(from <old-file>, header his)" exists for this file, and no header has changed since (confirmed via the 0e4f7c9e..HEAD diff, maintainer-block-only).
